chunks: ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

“ʿAqīqah is binding upon one who is wealthy, and whoever is poor, then when he becomes financially able, he should perform it. If he is not able to do that, then there is nothing upon him. If no ʿaqīqah was performed for him until an udḥiyyah was offered on his behalf, then the udḥiyyah has sufficed for him. Every newborn is held in pledge by his ʿaqīqah.”

And he said concerning the ʿaqīqah: “A ram is to be slaughtered on his behalf. If a ram is not found, whatever suffices in the udḥiyyah will suffice for him. Otherwise, then a lamb—the largest that may be found among the lambs of the year.”

key_terms.الْأُضْحِيَّةُ: the sacrificial animal offered for Eid al-Aḍḥā
key_terms.الْعَقِيقَةُ: the sacrificial offering made on behalf of a newborn
key_terms.مُرْتَهَنٌ: held in pledge or dependent upon

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on ʿaqīqah for the wealthy and the poor, and what animal suffices for it?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out the ruling of ʿaqīqah for a newborn, making it binding for the wealthy while excusing the one who lacks means until he becomes able. It also explains what type of animal is to be offered and states that an udḥiyyah may suffice if ʿaqīqah was not previously done.
